overview: Prospective observational study of structured reporting for abdominal and pelvic CT from 2027-01-11 to 2027-07-11, with a rated sample of free-text reports from the six months before as context.
population: Abdominal and pelvic CT reports for suspected appendicitis, bowel obstruction and cancer staging; referring surgeons and emergency physicians for the questionnaire.
exposure: The structured template with fixed headings and pick-lists.
procedures: Each month the registrar samples 25 reports per index question (75 a month) from the reporting system by random number, extracts template status (opened, completed, overridden) and rates key elements against the checklist. The same checklist is applied to 150 historic free-text reports with the stated-or-implied rule, fixed in advance. Active reporting time comes from system time stamps. A five-item referrer questionnaire is sent at months 3 and 6.

outcomes.name: All key elements present
outcomes.measure: Proportion of sampled reports containing every pre-specified key element for the clinical question

outcomes.name: Active reporting time
outcomes.measure: Median minutes from opening to sign-off
outcomes.why: No extra reporting time is available.

outcomes.name: Referrer usefulness rating
outcomes.why: Whether reports are easier to act on.

feasibility: Rating 75 reports a month at about 2 minutes each fits within 3 registrar hours a week.
biasMitigation: Stated-or-implied rule fixed before historic rating
Second rater on 10 percent of reports

biasFlags.label: Checklist designed with the template
biasFlags.note: Favours structured reports; historic comparison is context only.

parsimony.simplestPath: Monthly random samples, one checklist, time stamps and a short questionnaire.

summary: Six-month prospective study with monthly random samples and a fixed checklist.
